correctness.rationale: In the three-strategy well-mixed model, pivotal event for one protective rather than ordinary focal player requires exactly a=M−1 protective partners among n=N−1, leaving b=N−M nonprotective partners. Multinomial risk summation gives Ψρ=C(n,a)z^a[(1−z)^b−(ρ(1−z)+(1−ρ)x)^b], with 0≤ρ<1 and payoff advantage −k+LωΨρ. At fixed z, Ψ strictly decreases in x; boundary Ψ(0,z) is a positive multiple of z^a(1−z)^b, uniquely maximized at x=0,z=a/n. This proves k*=Lω(1−ρ^b)C(n,a)(a/n)^a(b/n)^b. Replicator d(log(z/x))/dt=−k+LωΨ and compactness rule out a positive asymptotic protective fraction at k=k* when both x,z initially positive; with z→0 Cesaro yields time-averaged log ratio −k. Uniform localization of the unique maximum and Taylor expansion Ψ/Ψ*=1−Hρ x−D(z−a/n)²+o(x+(z−a/n)²) for fixed positive ρ gives area 4ε^(3/2)/(3Hρ sqrt(D)). At ρ=0, derivative is x^b and gives beta-function coefficient (b/(n sqrt(D)))B(1/2,1+1/b)ε^(1/2+1/b). Independent exact small multinomial sums and numeric x-slice integrations for (n,a,ρ)=(4,2,.4),(5,2,.7),(4,2,0),(5,2,0),(4,3,0) gave observed/predicted ratios within .8% for ε=.01, tightening at .003. The all-parameter statement is proved by analysis; numeric finite slices are corroboration.
